quest.title: Dodoco's Boom-Bastic Escapades!
quest.description: While passing by a quiet garden in Mondstadt, a couple of Knights who are discussing a "new game" draw your and Paimon's attention...

dialogues.speaker: Ematol
dialogues.text: C'mon, Phonia, c'mon! Don't you want to be the first player to ever experience the marvel that is "Dodoco's Boom-Bastic Escapades"? Go on, you know you want to!

dialogues.speaker: Ematol
dialogues.text: An all-new combat mode that's more flexible than ever before, allowing you to not only achieve pinpoint-precise demolition but also outsmart crafty enemies while you're at it — how could that not be an absolute blast!

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: How about... no. Just because you spend all day fantasizing about bombs, doesn't mean the rest of us do too.

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: Heck, helping you out by getting the prototype and tabletop game up and running already counts as some serious overtime.

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: All I want to do now is order some takeout from the Good Hunter, then return to the comfort of my humble abode. By the time it arrives, I'll have just finished the last of the laundry, and it'll finally be time to kick back and relax...

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: As for this new boom shaka-lacking game of yours... Well, next time we're on shift together, I might give it a go. If I'm already bored out of my mind, what harm could it do anyway...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you just say the words "new" and "game" together in the same sentence? Paimon's curious now... Could we take a look?

dialogues.speaker: Ematol
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, is that you, Honorary Knight and their Helper in White? You're actually here! What are the chances!?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Y—You know who I am, Honorary Knight? I must really have left an impression during "Annihilate the Invasive Anglers"... Even you've heard about me?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: I—I—I... I promise I won't let you down!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Recently, I've been making ongoing improvements to the formula and design of my bombs, striving to narrow the gap between me and the Spark Knight, bit by bit, boom by boom...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Anyway, after the previous operation, Ematol concluded that relying solely on long-distance bomb deployment had considerable tactical shortcomings, and wasn't effective enough at dealing with certain types of obstacles and cover...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: So she began experimenting with some new equipment. To test it out, we even made some improvements to the Spark Knight's beloved tabletop game.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: That's right! And in recent days, after analyzing the Spark Knight's combat strategy, I've come up with another way to use the bombs!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: If we were the Spark Knight, the solution would probably be: "If a single bomb's worth of explosives isn't enough, use three; if a lone Jumpy Dumpty can't solve the issue, throw three." And yes, increased firepower is a surefire way to solve the problem.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: But for run-of-the-mill Knights like us, that just isn't an option. We simply can't compete with the Spark Knight's Jumpy Dumpties and their boom factor, so we've focused on improving flexibility and accuracy to make up for the lack of power.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Our thinking was that if we could create something that could track targets and get close enough to lay down bombs, we could strike dangerous targets with pinpoint accuracy and thereby maximize the load!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: T—Tracking enemies and laying down bombs? Sounds pretty impressive, but also kinda scary...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Paimon were a hilichurl chasing down a Forest Boar with her hilichurl buddies, and suddenly a little thingamajig popped out of nowhere and threw a bomb in our faces... she'd probably be so terrified she'd faint!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're spot on... the fact that it would be so terrifying to monsters and enemies simply proves how useful it would be to us, the Knights of Favonius, and upstanding adventurers too!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: But this new device is still in the early stages of testing. It'll take some time before it's ready for official production and use... I'll give it everything I've got!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Given that conducting experiments in the wild would harm Mondstadt's natural ecosystem and how this isn't important enough to justify us bothering Captain Albedo, it wasn't worth the trouble of applying for a testing ground.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: After Ematol asked for my advice, we settled on a small-scale simulation prototype to test the controls and explosive capabilities.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: It just so happened that we thought of an old tabletop game that would make the perfect foundation for such testing. So Ematol dragged me off to find Lisa...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: And thank goodness we did! With Lisa's enthusiastic support, advice, and even some help with the storyline, the end result is... a-ma-zing!!!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Tada! Behold, here on this game table before your very eyes, the much-awaited sequel to Dodoco's Bomb-Tastic Adventure... "Dodoco's Boom-Bastic Escapades"!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: After mastering the art of close-range demolition, Dodoco and her Special Jumpy Dumpties are back with an explosively volatile vengeance, here to follow our commands and obliterate hordes of resurgent enemies!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Bear witness to an epic battle of wits between Dodoco and the Spikey Fish King, and as you do, immerse yourself in intense action and joyous destruction... while helping us record valuable test data for our new device, of course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! So that's the game you've been working on, huh, Ematol? The latest installment in the Dodoco versus Spikey Fish saga!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Seems like the Honorary Knight and the Helper in White are pretty excited about it, Ematol. Their feedback will no doubt prove invaluable.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: I can tell! If they'd be willing to spend some of their precious time playing, I'd be eternally grateful!

choices.text: Does that mean we'll be the first to play it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Given that it's the follow-up to the Dodoco v. Spikey Fish story, wouldn't the Spark Knight herself be the most suitable game tester of all?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Ah! Well... Considering that Dodoco features in the new game, that would of course be a true honor...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: But I wanted to make sure that "Dodoco's Boom-Bastic Escapades" is as incredible an experience as possible, with as few flaws as is humanly possible, such that by the time the Spark Knight gets the chance to play it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon's got it! You're saying that this time, we'll have multiple roles — not only are we helping you test out your new device, but we're also acting as game testers, making sure that Klee will love it!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Wonderful! I'd say we're getting on like an exploding house on fire, wouldn't you agree?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Just the thought of watching you guys play gets me so pumped right now! Anyway, let's get this show on the road!

choices.text: In the name of Klee, and fun games too!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: My hunch was right! You're an explosives enthusiast, just like me...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Mere cogs in the well-oiled machine that is the Knights of Favonius that we are, it's no surprise that you haven't heard of us, Honorary Knight, or that our faces might have slipped your mind. Perfectly understandable!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: I'm Phonia, Investigative Team Signals Officer, and I'm responsible for testing alchemical detection equipment. This is my colleague, Investigative Team Weapons Officer Ematol, who has a... shall we say, rather unique interest in explosives.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Last time, we were in charge of dealing with those Anglers from Sumeru invading Cider Lake. That operation, which took place quite a while back now, went pretty smoothly.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: After that, Ematol concluded that relying solely on long-distance bomb deployment had considerable tactical shortcomings, and wasn't effective enough at dealing with certain types of obstacles and cover...
